**For most flyers, I'd get the Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W).** If you only need to charge a phone, the smaller Baseus PicoGo AM52 is the cheaper pick. The comparison I found covers only these two Baseus models, so this isn't a full survey of the market.

## Picks

- **Baseus Blade H1, $89.99:** At about 74 Wh, it's under the 100 Wh limit. It can charge a laptop and a phone, with 100 W USB-C output and 2 USB-C and 2 USB-A ports. It's a good fit if you want one bank for everything. [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah) (source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-power-bank-for-airplane-travel-2026-airline-lithium-battery-carry-on-rules-)).
- **Baseus PicoGo AM52, $53.99 with code AM52 (otherwise $59.99):** At about 37 Wh, it has a 10,000 mAh capacity. It does magnetic wireless charging for iPhones (25 W on iPhone 16 or later, 15 W on iPhone 12 to 15) and 45 W wired output. If you don't have an iPhone, the Blade H1 is the better fit. [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w) (source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-power-bank-for-airplane-travel-2026-airline-lithium-battery-carry-on-rules-)).

Both are affiliate links, so Dealectric is paid if you buy. The code was last tested on 2026-10-24, so confirm the price at checkout.

## Rules for any power bank on a plane

- **Carry-on only:** Spare lithium batteries and power banks can't go in checked bags. If your bag is gate-checked, take the power bank out first ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- **Under 100 Wh:** That covers nearly all consumer power banks. With airline approval you can carry up to two larger ones (101-160 Wh). To check a bank's rating, multiply volts by amp-hours ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)).
- **Protect the terminals:** Keep the bank in its original packaging, a pouch, or a case, or tape over the terminals ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- **Airlines can be stricter:** Southwest, for example, limits each customer to one power bank as of April 20, 2026. It also can't be charged from in-seat power, and it must be visible while in use rather than stored in a bag ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)). Check your airline's policy before you fly.

Do you know which airline you're flying and what you'll be charging? I can narrow the pick down from there.
